claims.text: Solution-treated and quenched HfNbTaTiZr has a homogeneous single-phase BCC matrix without secondary phases.
A minor Al addition combined with optimized aging will promote coherent nanoscale precipitates in HfNbTaTiZr.
The precipitates produced by Al addition and aging will enhance both strength and plasticity relative to the single-phase reference alloy.
A solution treatment near 1200°C followed by quenching and aging near 800°C for 1–3 hours is an appropriate processing route for the Al-modified alloy.
Al must be fully dissolved during the high-temperature treatment for controlled precipitation during aging.
Excessive Al or unsuitable aging can produce brittle intermetallic phases.
The targeted structural mediator is a fine distribution of coherent nanometer-sized precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The precipitates may have an L12 or ordered-BCC structure.
The nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the alloy through an Orowan mechanism.
Coherent precipitate interfaces and a controlled precipitate volume fraction facilitate dislocation absorption and emission.
Dislocation absorption and emission at the precipitate interfaces enhance strain hardening and preserve or improve ductility.
The Al-doped and heat-treated alloy will have higher yield strength than the single-phase reference alloy.
The Al-doped and heat-treated alloy will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the single-phase reference alloy.
The Al-doped and heat-treated alloy will retain comparable or slightly improved plastic strain to failure.
The intervention should also be effective in refractory high-entropy alloys having similar BCC matrices and high melting temperatures.
The intervention may lose effectiveness when the Al level exceeds its optimum or when aging is not precisely controlled.
Precipitation hardening is a well-established strengthening mechanism.

contradictions.description: The reference condition is inconsistent: the material initial state is solution-treated and quenched, the main hypothesis and predicted outcome refer to an as-cast reference, and the baseline permits either an as-cast or quenched alloy. These are distinct processing states and do not define one unambiguous comparator.
